absent: Numeric value and bit layout of the frozen marker and frozen detection predicate.
Full struct layouts beyond observed fields for page, iterator, VM, slot, request, filter, notifier, file and inode objects.
Inner change-accounting behavior behind the checked helper invoked on every entry update.
Semantics of shadow predicates and helpers for present, last-level, atomic-need, mirror, virtualization-exception, entry counts and huge-page scaling.
Deferred page freeing, vendor mirror release, tracing, bug and warning macro effects, and accounting helpers.
Root-type enum values and full root lifecycle outside invalidation, including creation, zapping and reference handling.
Iterator creation, traversal, progress-frame updates, flush and scheduling helper effects, and recovery after yield.
Memory-slot install, overlap-check, address-space count, max pages, slot-number limits, change-type values and flag values.
User mapping, unmapping, tagging, accessibility-check and page-size constant semantics.
Guest-file operations, binding table semantics, file lookup and reference handling, release path, file-state lock scope, and mappable-flag value.

findings.text: Internal memory region helper creates or deletes a host-chosen mapping in every address space. Creation fails when the identifier is out of range or a populated slot already exists, otherwise it obtains a shared anonymous host mapping and installs it through the internal slot path. Deletion is a no-op returning null when no populated slot exists, otherwise it uninstalls from every address space and then releases the host mapping.

Generic memory region installer validates flags, alignment, user address accessibility, address-space and slot bounds, guest address wrapping and size limits, then dispatches to create, move, flags-only or delete paths. Creation checks total page-count overflow and overlap with existing slots. Modification rejects address, size or protection changes except narrowly allowed move and flag updates, with guest-private slots immutable except for deletion.

Root invalidation scans the VM root list and, for each root matching the requested direct or mirror and validity selection, marks it invalid and flags it for scheduled zapping if not already invalid. Invalid-only request bits are stripped with a developer warning. The operation expects exclusive MMU lock protection whenever the VM has users and created vCPUs, with the check waived during destruction.

Guest-private binding associates a new invisible memory slot with a file range and later dissociates it. Binding validates file descriptor type and VM ownership, offset alignment and file-size containment, and rejects overlapping ranges before publishing the file pointer and start offset and recording the range. Unbinding is null-safe, removes the recorded range and nullifies the published pointer, using the file-state lock for live files and lock-free removal when the file is already dying.

Page-track teardown has two builds: a full build that releases the notifier head synchronization structure, and a no-op inline build that does nothing. The choice is compile-time per translation unit.
MSR filter destructor is null-safe. For a non-null filter it releases each per-range bitmap up to the recorded count and then releases the filter object itself.

Small accessors centralize shadow entry reads and writes under read-copy-update protection. Reads use a single volatile read. One write path always exchanges atomically while rejecting a virtualization-exception-sensitive value, and another write path selects atomic exchange only when the old value and level require it, otherwise using a plain protected store and returning the prior value.

Slot lookup helpers expose the default address-space table and hash lookup by numeric identifier. The default table is address space zero, and lookup scans the identifier hash chain for an exact identifier match, returning null when absent.

Two install paths exist for shadow entries during iteration. The exclusive path requires exclusive MMU lock ownership, refuses frozen values on either side, performs the protected write, applies change accounting, and returns the prior value while updating the iterator snapshot. The atomic path uses compare-exchange, refreshes the iterator snapshot on contention to allow retry, signals busy on loss, and warns if the iterator had yielded or the snapshot was frozen.

Removal of a page-table page first unlinks and accounts the page, then walks every entry computing its guest frame from base plus index scaled by level. The shared path repeatedly exchanges toward the frozen marker until it replaces a non-frozen value. The exclusive path skips non-present entries including emulated IO entries and otherwise freezes present entries with the protected write. Every visited index then undergoes uniform change accounting toward frozen, with mirror pages additionally released through the vendor hook before deferred freeing.

Atomic shadow-entry update is required exactly when the old entry is present in the shadow sense, is a last-level entry for the given level, and carries hardware-updated state that needs atomicity. All other combinations permit a plain protected store.

An iterator needs to yield only when scheduler or lock fairness signals pressure and forward progress has occurred since the last yield, measured by a change in the next last-level guest frame versus the yielded frame. A yield flushes remote translation buffers when requested, drops read-copy-update protection, yields the appropriate lock mode, retakes protection, validates monotonic progress, and marks the iterator yielded.

Root selection rejects empty valid-type requests with a developer warning. Invalid roots are excluded unless invalid types are explicitly requested. Non-mirror roots match direct requests and mirror roots match mirror requests, with direct being the expected fast path.

Region validation requires page-aligned size and guest address, page-aligned and untagged user address that passes accessibility checks for the full size, address-space and slot bounds, no guest-address wrapping, and user-slot page-count caps. Guest-private regions additionally require page-aligned file offset without size wrapping. Flag changes are limited to defined bits with dirty logging, guest-private and read-only interactions constrained by build options and architecture support.

Internal slot installation rejects user-space slot numbers and any nonzero flags before delegating to the generic installer. When binding guest-private memory backed by a mappable file, the slot gains an internal guest-only marker in addition to the requested flags.

Unlinking a shadow page always unaccounts one page-table page and, under a debug build, decrements the VM page counter. Huge-page tracking is touched only when the disallowed flag is set: the flag is cleared under the page-tracking spin lock and the page is removed from huge-page tracking for the two-dimensional paging mode.
When guest-private memory support is compiled out, binding and unbinding helpers do not touch slot or file state; they emit a developer warning and binding reports an input-output failure.

Exclusive shadow-entry installation and root invalidation on a live VM require the MMU lock held for write. Iteration yielding must distinguish shared versus exclusive ownership to yield the matching lock mode. The atomic install path is intended for read-mode lock holders and concurrent fast-fault writers outside the lock, using compare-exchange rather than exclusive assertion.

Internal region management and generic region installation require the slots lock held. Guest-private binding and live unbinding serialize range-table changes under the file invalidation lock, while unbinding a dying file relies on slots-lock exclusion instead because release cannot complete until that lock is dropped. Page unlink serialization for huge-page state uses a dedicated spin lock.

Shadow-entry pointers are dereferenced under read-copy-update protection. Writes that can race with other virtual CPUs or fast faults use atomic exchange or compare-exchange. Iteration that yields must exit read-copy-update protection before scheduling and re-enter it afterwards, and must not assume entry stability across the yield.

Shadow paging state centers on a page object carrying level and validity in its role, a base guest frame, a table pointer, a deferred-free callback head, linkage for the root list, a scheduled-zap flag, a huge-page disallowed flag and a mirror indicator. Iteration state carries the current entry pointer and snapshot, guest frame and level, yielded and progress frames, and a yielded flag that blocks unsafe reuse.

Memory-slot state carries address-space and slot identifiers, base guest frame, page count, flags, user address and optional guest-file binding with offset. The user request carries a packed slot identifier, flags, guest address, user address, size and optional guest-file descriptor with offset. Lookup uses a per-table hash keyed by identifier with a node index selecting the hash node.

Ancillary state includes an MSR filter with a range count and per-range bitmaps, a page-track notifier head with a synchronization structure, a VM with slots and MMU locks plus user and vCPU counts and total slot pages, and a guest-file inode wrapper exposing flags including a mappable indicator that drives the guest-only slot marker.

Shadow-entry zapping moves each entry toward a frozen marker and then through change accounting. Shared owners spin on frozen values to avoid clobbering concurrent faults, exclusive owners skip non-present entries, and both converge on frozen before accounting. The parent page is unlinked before children are processed and freed only after a grace period, with mirror backing released before that deferral.

Roots move from valid to invalid plus scheduled-zap exactly once, remain on the list while invalid, and must be zapped before a slot update completes even though references may keep them alive afterwards. Iterators move from running to yielded on scheduling pressure with forward progress, and yielded state forbids atomic install and further conditional yield without refresh.

Slots move through create, move or flags-only update, and delete, with no-op when nothing changes. Internal regions couple host mapping lifetime to slot lifetime: map then install on create, uninstall then unmap on delete. Guest bindings move from absent to range-recorded plus file-published, then back to range-cleared plus file-nulled on unbind or file release, with private slots otherwise immutable.

After a parent entry is made non-present but before translation buffers are flushed, hardware address and dirty assists may still walk cached upper entries and dirty a child. A non-atomic child update could therefore drop a dirty indication, and a simple dirty-bit pre-check is insufficient because a fast fault can make the child writable and resume the guest between the read and the write. The exclusive zap path therefore uses the protected atomic-aware write even though it holds the write lock.

Overwriting a frozen entry through the normal path, installing to or from frozen through the exclusive path, or reusing a yielded iterator without refresh risks lost updates or stale snapshots. The implementation guards these with developer warnings on frozen values and yielded state, a monotonic guest-frame check after yielding, and a busy signal with snapshot refresh on compare-exchange contention so callers retry on fresh data.

Region handling must reject overlapping guest ranges, guest-address and file-offset wrapping, total page-count overflow, misaligned or tagged or inaccessible user addresses, mismatched modify parameters, and double binding of the same file range. File-descriptor mixups such as non-guest files or files owned by another VM, and oversized offsets beyond file size, must also fail rather than install a binding. Fallback guest-memory stubs unconditionally warn and fail.

The slot identifier is a packed value with the low sixteen bits holding the slot number and the upper bits holding the address-space number. Sizes, guest addresses, user addresses and guest-file offsets are page-granular, and internal slots occupy numeric identifiers at or above the user-slot limit while all identifiers stay below the global slot maximum.

User-pointer error returns encode a negative errno value as a user-tagged pointer constant, used to report invalid identifier, existing slot, mapping failure and per-address-space install failures from the internal region helper.
